transcript:
Jo: How was your interview at the neighborhood museum on Friday, Rina?
Rina: It was interesting. I went at eleven in the morning and spoke to the manager of the events department.
Jo: What position did you apply for?
Rina: The vacancy was for a weekend workshop assistant. I sent the application on Wednesday. The employer wanted someone to help visitors find materials.
Jo: Did you give an example of your experience?
Rina: Yes. I described a garden event where my colleague and I worked as a team. I showed a certificate from a short art course as one qualification. I also brought a copy of my application for the manager.
Jo: What did they ask about?
Rina: They asked how I would help a customer who arrived late. I said I would listen, check the task list and ask an employee if I was unsure.
Jo: Did they explain the pay?
Rina: Yes. The hourly wage was fourteen pounds. The manager also mentioned a monthly salary, but that was for a different full-time position.
Jo: Did you get a decision at the interview?
Rina: No. They will contact each candidate next Tuesday. My goal was to speak clearly, and I felt successful in giving my example.
Jo: What will you do while you wait?
Rina: I will resume my library volunteering on Sunday. I enjoy that service, and I want to build a reliable work routine for my career.
Jo: Did you ask about the first responsibility?
Rina: Yes. A new assistant starts by preparing tables before visitors arrive. I wrote it in my notes, because this opportunity could teach me a new skill.
